Plot a scatterplot of two or three variables, optionally split by group

Source: R/plotscat.R
plotscat.Rd

Plots x against y, with a regression line, and puts the correlation statistics in the plot title. What happens depends on z:

Usage

plotscat(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  z = NULL,
  cl = 2,
  condcols = NULL,
  cleand = FALSE,
  results_title = TRUE,
  title_text = NULL,
  outp = "analysis",
  w = 6,
  h = 6,
  label = NULL,
  bayes_factor = F
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the columns to be plotted, one row per participant.

x

Name of the column for the x axis.

y

Name of the column for the y axis.

z

Optional name of a third column, either numeric or a grouping factor.

cl

For a grouping factor: 2 draws a regression line for each group, 1 draws one line for everyone.

condcols

Colours for the groups when z is a grouping factor. By default they are chosen by replacecondcols().

cleand

If TRUE, remove rows with missing values first.

results_title

Show the statistics in the plot title?

title_text

Optional extra text for the top of the title.

outp

Name of the folder in which to save the plot as a pdf (it is created if needed). Set to NULL or "" to not save.

w

Width of the saved plot, in inches.

h

Height of the saved plot, in inches.

label

Optional name of a column to use to label each point.

bayes_factor

Calculate Bayes factors? This needs the BayesFactor package. The Bayes factors are shown in the plot title.

Value

A list containing the plot (p) and the statistics: r, p value, Bayes factor and Kendall's tau for each correlation, the p value for the difference between the correlations (cc), and the interaction Bayes factor (intbf), when relevant.

Details

  • no z: just y against x.

  • z is a number: y and z are both plotted against x, in different colours, and the two correlations are compared, using cocor (Hittner et al., 2003).

  • z is a factor or text: y against x is plotted separately for each group in z (only the first two groups are used), and the two correlations are compared (see plotscat_split).

See also

singlecor(), exclorr()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plotscat(mtcars, x = "mpg", y = "hp", outp = NULL)
plotscat(mtcars, x = "mpg", y = "hp", z = "am", outp = NULL)
} # }
